Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3316); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite:--Jephthah.
BiblicalUsage: Jephthah was a judge of Israel, and Hebrews names him once, in the hall of faith. In Hebrews 11:32 the writer says time would fail him to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae, and of David, and of Samuel, and of the prophets.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jephthah's place in that list is grace itself: a flawed man with a rash vow, named among the faithful because he believed God in the battle.
RelatedPeople: Jephthah, Judge of Israel; Gideon; Samson; King David; Samuel
RelatedEvents: Samson and Delilah; Gideon's Victory over Midian
